memory_update.text: ZBRA should remain the reference auto-ID hardware leader for RFID/barcode readers, printers, mobile computing, and retail workflow context, but it is not the main underfollowed discovery candidate.
PI is a high-purity underfollowed candidate for RAIN RFID component/platform exposure tied to item-level retail inventory, apparel, supply-chain/logistics, and loss-prevention adoption.
AVY is a large-cap but relevant materials/consumables candidate because RFID inlays, smart labels, apparel tags, and fresh-food RFID labels sit close to mandate-driven recurring label demand.
SPSC is a hypothesis-stage underfollowed software/network candidate for supplier compliance, EDI, trading-partner maps, and retailer-specific integration logic adjacent to RFID/labeling mandates.

Layer 2 should verify direct mandate exposure: Walmart/Target/apparel/fresh-food programs, segment revenue contribution, customer concentration, recurring consumables versus hardware/software mix, and whether demand is compliance-mandated rather than discretionary IT spend.

node: RFID, barcode, labeling, serialization, and retailer compliance infrastructure
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the RFID/barcode/labeling/retail-compliance infrastructure node found four US-listed candidates: one obvious reference leader in auto-ID hardware, one large-cap label/materials supplier, one purer underfollowed RAIN RFID component/platform company, and one underfollowed retail supplier-compliance network/software company. The bottleneck hypothesis remains plausible: if retailer mandates broaden, value may accrue to certified tags, inlays, readers, printers, middleware, supplier onboarding, and compliance logic rather than only to retailers. Claims are intentionally early-stage and require later verification against segment revenue, customer concentration, mandate-driven orders, and margin sensitivity.
